extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and patent office officials (U.S.)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards and procedural requirements from the U.S. Patent Acts of 1836, 1837, and 1839 governing patent validity, prosecution, defenses, remedies, office procedure, and administrative duties. Includes statutory criteria for evidence, disclaimers, reissues, extensions, prior use, and other substantive rules for patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of annexed description and specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions and specifications annexed to an original application upon payment (e.g., fifteen dollars) shall be certified by the Commissioner as to time of annexation and recorded, and thereafter "have the same effect in law ... as though it had been embraced in the original description and specification."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annexed material, if properly recorded and fee paid, is treated as part of the original filing for all legal intents and purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court discretion to award enhanced damages in infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever, in any action for damages for making, using, or selling the thing patented, a verdict is rendered for the plaintiff, the court may render judgment for any sum above the amount found by such verdict as the actual damages sustained by the plaintiff, "not exceeding three times the amount thereof, according to the circumstances of the case, with costs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts have discretion to increase damages up to treble based on case circumstances; costs may also be awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant's right to plead general issue and give special matter in evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The defendant may plead the general issue and give this act and any special matter in evidence, of which notice in writing may have been given to the plaintiff or his attorney thirty days before trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defendant must give written notice 30 days before trial to rely on special matter; allows statutory and fact-based defenses to be introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated substantive defenses to infringement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Defenses permitting judgment for the defendant include that the plaintiff's specification and claim "does not contain the whole truth relative to his invention ... or ... contains more than is necessary to produce the described effect" (concealment or addition made to deceive), that the patentee was not the "original and first inventor or discoverer" of the thing or a substantial part claimed, that it "had been described in some public work anterior" to the patentee, that it "had been in public use or on sale with the consent and allowance of the patentee before his application," that the patent was "surreptitiously or unjustly obtained" from another who was reasonably diligent, or that an alien patentee failed for eighteen months to put the invention on sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are multiple substantive grounds that can render a patent unenforceable in a damages action; proof must show the stated facts (e.g., prior publication, prior use/sale, fraud, lack of originality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant's obligation when relying on prior invention/knowledge/use
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the defendant relies in his defence on the fact of a previous invention, knowledge, or use of the thing patented, he shall state, in his notice of special matter, the names and places of residence of those whom he intends to prove to have possessed a prior knowledge of the thing, and where the same had been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must identify witnesses and locations for proof of prior knowledge/use to preserve the defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proviso protecting good-faith belief of first invention against foreign prior knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever it satisfactorily appears that the patentee, at the time of making his application, believed himself to be the first inventor, the patent shall not be held void on account of the invention having been before known or used in any foreign country, provided it does not appear that the same had before been patented or described in any printed publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good-faith belief of being first may avoid invalidation based on foreign prior use unless there was a prior patent or printed publication abroad that anticipates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court powers when plaintiff's claim embraces more than actual invention
rubrics_metrics.description: If the plaintiff fails on the ground that his specification of claim "is embraced more than that of which he was the first inventor," but the defendant used any part "justly and truly specified and claimed as new," the court may adjudge and award costs as may appear just and equitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when an overbroad claim causes plaintiff to fail, courts can award equitable costs where defendant infringed a legitimately claimed subset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for interfering patents and adverse examiner decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: When there are two interfering patents, or a patent on application refused as interfering with an unexpired prior patent, any interested person may have remedy by bill in equity; the court may adjudge patents void in whole or in part, inoperative or invalid in any particular part or portion of the United States, and may adjudge that an applicant is entitled to a patent for his invention (or part) according to proof of priority; such adjudications affect only the parties and those deriving title from them subsequent to the judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity suits can resolve priority/interference disputes; courts may both cancel and award patent rights depending on priority and interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal jurisdiction and equitable remedies in patent cases
rubrics_metrics.description: All actions, suits, controversies, and cases arising under U.S. laws granting exclusive rights to inventors shall be originally cognizable in the circuit courts of the United States (or district courts with circuit powers); such courts may grant injunctions according to equity, and appeals (writs of error) may be taken to the Supreme Court as in other cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent disputes are federal; equitable relief (injunctions) and appellate review are available under established procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and criteria for patent term extension
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee desiring an extension beyond the patent term may apply in writing to the Commissioner, pay forty dollars, and the Commissioner shall publish notice in principal newspapers (and other papers deemed proper) of time/place for consideration so any person may appear to show cause against extension. The Secretary of State, the Commissioner, and the Solicitor of the Treasury shall form a board to hear evidence for and against extension. The patentee must furnish under oath a statement of the ascertained value of the invention and of receipts and expenditures in detail. If the board, with due regard to public interest, is fully satisfied that extension is just because the patentee (without neglect or fault) failed to obtain reasonable remuneration, the Commissioner shall renew/extend the patent by certificate for seven years after expiration of the first term; extension benefits assignees/grantees; no extension after expiration of the original term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension requires formal application, fee, public notice, a three-member board hearing, sworn financial disclosure, and a public-interest judgment; extension is seven years and must be granted before expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for Patent Office library and appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be provided for the Patent Office a library of scientific works and periodicals, foreign and American, to facilitate duties of chief officers, to be purchased under Library of Congress committee direction; appropriation of fifteen hundred dollars from the patent fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory mandate for establishing and funding a technical library to support patent examination and administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification, preservation, and public display of models and specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner must cause models and specimens (patented or unpatented) deposited in the office to be classified and arranged in suitable rooms or galleries, preserved when necessary, and displayed in a manner conducive to beneficial public inspection; rooms/galleries to be kept open during suitable hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent models and specimens must be curated and made available for public inspection under the Commissioner's supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal of prior acts with saving clauses and transitional treatment of pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: All prior acts on this subject are repealed; however, actions/processes pending prior to passage may be prosecuted to final judgment as if the act had not passed, excepting application of certain sections where applicable; applications/petitions for patents pending at passage where duty paid shall be proceeded with as though filed after passage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeals include transitional safeguards preserving pending rights and proceedings subject to specified provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording of pre-December 15, 1836 patents and documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person in possession or interest in a patent issued prior to Dec 15, 1836 (or assignments executed/recorded prior) may, without charge, present them to the Commissioner to have them recorded anew with descriptions, specifications, claims, and drawings; the Commissioner shall transcribe authenticated copies into record books; where drawings were not originally annexed, a drawing verified by oath may be filed or copied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners of pre-fire patents can have records reconstructed and entered anew to restore the evidentiary record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copies as prima facie evidence; recording requirement for admissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of such records and drawings certified by the Commissioner (or chief clerk in his absence) shall be prima facie evidence of particulars of the invention and patent in U.S. courts where originals would be evidence; no patent issued prior to Dec 15 shall be received in evidence on behalf of the patentee after the following June 1 unless it has been so recorded anew and a drawing (if separate) verified and deposited; likewise written assignments recorded prior to that date must be recorded anew to be received in evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording reconstructed certified copies is necessary to make pre-fire patents admissible in court after the statutory deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue for patents destroyed or lost (same original date)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent was destroyed by the burning of the Patent Office or otherwise lost, the Commissioner shall, on application by the patentee and deposit of a duplicate model/drawings/description verified by oath as required, issue a new patent for the same invention bearing the date of the original patent and enter it of record; such patent and certified copies shall be admissible as evidence and protect rights to the extent of the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lost/destroyed patents can be reissued with original date upon verified replacement submissions; evidentiary effect and scope are limited to original protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement of duplicate models destroyed by fire and temporary board
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner must procure duplicates of models destroyed by fire that were most valuable/important to the public and to issuing patents; a temporary board (Commissioner + two presidential appointees) is to consider best mode of obtaining suitable models and may establish regulations; reasonable expense may be incurred but total not to exceed $100,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory authorization and budget cap for replacing valuable models lost in the Patent Office fire; a small board to oversee procurement and rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and requirements for multiple reissue patents and deposit of duplicate models
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent is returned for correction and reissue and the patentee desires several patents for distinct separate parts of the thing patented, he shall pay an additional sum (thirty dollars for each additional patent). No patent made prior to Dec 15 shall be corrected and reissued until a duplicate of the model and drawing verified by oath is deposited; no addition of an improvement to any patent previously granted or new patent for an improvement made to the original inventor shall be admitted until a duplicate model/drawing of the thing as originally invented is deposited if required by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue and divisional-like issuance for separate parts requires fees and, where models were lost, verified duplicates before recordation/reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to furnish duplicate drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: In all cases hereafter, the applicant for a patent shall furnish duplicate drawings whenever the case admits of drawings, one to be deposited in the office and the other to be annexed to the patent and considered part of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two copies of drawings: one for the office record and one attached to the patent itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to make disclaimer for overbroad claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a patentee has by inadvertence, accident, or mistake claimed more than he was the original or first inventor of, he (or his administrators, executors, assigns) may make a disclaimer of such parts not claimed to be held by virtue of the patent, stating extent of interest; the disclaimer shall be in writing, attested by witnesses, recorded in the Patent Office on payment of ten dollars, and thereafter taken as part of the original specification to extent of interest. Such disclaimer shall not affect actions pending at the time except as relates to unreasonable neglect or delay in filing the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclaimers can narrow asserted scope to remove overclaims; formal execution, fee, and recordation are required; timing relative to suits matters for costs and relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision and restriction of claims on additions/improvements and reissues
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever application is made for adding a newly discovered improvement to an existing patent, or a patent is returned for reissue, the specification of claim annexed shall be subject to revision and restriction in the same manner as original applications; the Commissioner shall not add the improvement nor grant the reissue until the applicant has entered a disclaimer or altered the specification of claim in accordance with the Commissioner's decision; applicant dissatisfied has the same remedy and privileges as in original applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims for improvements or reissues are examined and may be restricted; applicants have appeal/remedy channels analogous to originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of innocent mistake claiming unowned invention
rubrics_metrics.description: If, without wilful default or intent to defraud, a patentee mistakenly claimed to be the original and first inventor of a material or substantial part of the thing patented of which he was not the first inventor, the patent shall be deemed good and valid for so much of the invention as shall be bona fide his own (provided it is material and substantially distinguishable). Such patentee may maintain suit for infringement of that bona fide part, but to recover costs must have entered a disclaimer at the Patent Office prior to suit; and no person shall be entitled to benefits of this section if they unreasonably neglected or delayed to enter the disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innocent overclaiming does not wholly void a patent; rights persist for the true, distinguishable, owned portion but procedural steps (disclaimer) affect entitlement to costs and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner authorized to appoint agents for receiving models
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may appoint agents, not exceeding twenty, in principal cities or towns to receive and forward to the Patent Office models, specimens, and manufactures intended to be patented or deposited therein; transportation to be charged to the patent fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decentralized intake of physical exhibits is permitted via statutory agents to facilitate filings nationwide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and compensation of examining and copying clerks
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of one examining clerk there shall be appointed two examining clerks each receiving an annual salary (e.g., fifteen hundred dollars), and an additional copying clerk at a specified salary; the Commissioner may employ temporary clerks as necessary who shall receive specified per-page compensation (e.g., seven cents per 100 words) and reasonable compensation for drawings and record comparisons as prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staffing levels, positions, and compensation formulas for Patent Office clerical and examining personnel are statutorily set or authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund to foreign applicants rejected for lack of novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application of any foreigner for a patent is rejected and withdrawn for want of novelty pursuant to statutory provisions, the certificate of the Commissioner shall be a sufficient warrant to the treasurer to pay back two-thirds of the duty paid on account of such application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial refund mechanism for foreign applicants found non-novel by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmation in lieu of oath for conscientious scruples
rubrics_metrics.description: In all cases where an oath is required by this act or the prior act, if the person is conscientiously scrupulous of taking an oath, affirmation may be substituted therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious or conscientious objection allows affirmation rather than oath for statutory declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent fund accounting and annual reporting duties of Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: All moneys paid into the Treasury for patents and fees prior to the additional act shall be credited to the patent fund; the Commissioner may draw on the fund for necessary sums subject to limitations; he must lay before Congress each January a detailed statement of expenditures/payments from the fund and a list of all patents granted during the preceding year (subjects and alphabetical list of patentees and residences), and a list of patents that became public property during the same period, plus other useful information on the Patent Office's state and condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory financial oversight and annual reporting obligations to Congress for transparency and record-keeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of assistant examiners and temporary clerks (1839 provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be appointed two assistant examiners (each with an annual salary specified, e.g., twelve hundred fifty dollars) and the Commissioner is authorized to employ temporary clerks as needed; compensation for temporary clerks shall not exceed the rate charged for copies furnished by the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further staffing authorizations and compensation constraints to manage increased examination workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and distribution of classified patent list
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner is authorized to publish a classified and alphabetical list of all patents granted by the Patent Office previous to such publication, retain 100 copies for the Office and deposit 900 copies in the Library of Congress; up to $1,000 from the patent fund is appropriated for this expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory authorization and budget for producing a published patent catalog for distribution and archival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prior foreign patent or foreign publication on U.S. patentability (1839)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall be debarred from receiving a U.S. patent by reason of the same having been patented in a foreign country more than six months prior to his application, provided the invention "shall not have been introduced into public and common use in the United States" prior to the application; in such cases the U.S. patent shall be limited to a term of fourteen years from the date or publication of the foreign letters-patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign patenting more than six months before U.S. filing does not automatically bar U.S. patentability unless the invention was already in public/common use in the U.S.; limited term applies tied to foreign patent date/publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of prior purchasers/users before inventor's application
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person or corporation who purchased or constructed any newly invented machine, manufacture, or composition of matter prior to the inventor's application shall have the right to use and vend the specific thing so made or purchased without liability to the inventor, and no patent shall be held invalid by reason of such prior purchase, sale, or use except on proof of abandonment to the public or that such purchase/sale/use has been for more than two years prior to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good-faith prior users/purchasers have a statutory right to continue use/sale; the inventor's later patent does not impose liability absent abandonment or long prior use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abolition of recording fee for assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory requirement to pay three dollars to the Commissioner for recording any assignment, grant, or conveyance of interest under any patent is repealed; such instruments shall be recorded in future without any charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording assignments at the Patent Office is free of the previously required fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of interference/appeal remedies to refusals for any reason and applicant expense rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions extending remedies for interference and adverse decisions (section 16 previously) shall apply to all cases where patents are refused for any reason by the Commissioner or Chief Justice on appeals; in cases with no opposing party a copy of the bill shall be served on the Commissioner and the applicant shall pay all expenses of the proceeding whether final decision is in his favor or otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants challenging refusals may pursue equitable remedies but bear costs where no opposing party exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to appeal to Chief Justice of D.C. instead of board of examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an appeal is allowed by law from the Commissioner's decision to a board of examiners, the party may instead have a right to appeal to the Chief Justice of the U.S. district court for the District of Columbia by giving notice to the Commissioner and filing in the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative appellate route from Patent Office decisions to the judiciary (Chief Justice of D.C. district) is statutorily available upon procedure.
